text: Coral is not a rock and not a plant. Each piece of a reef is built by a tiny soft animal, a relative of the sea anemone, that makes a hard stony case around its body. Millions of those cases, piled up over hundreds of years, are what a reef is made of.

When something is under pressure it is being squeezed or strained and may not hold out much longer. Nothing is physically pressing on these reefs. The phrase means several forces at once are making life hard for them: hotter water, pollution and overfishing.

Acidic describes a liquid like lemon juice or vinegar, the sour kind that slowly eats away at chalky things such as eggshells and seashells. Chemists measure how acidic a liquid is on a scale. Seawater is not acidic yet, but carbon dioxide from the air is dissolving into it and pushing it that way, which makes life harder for animals that build hard skeletons.

Your comfort zone is the range of conditions you can handle happily. For a person that usually means familiar situations. For coral it means a real range of temperature and water chemistry it can survive in, and going outside that range does not just bother coral, it can kill it.

An algal bloom is a sudden population explosion of algae, the simple plant-like living things that float in water or coat rocks. Blooms happen when extra nutrients wash into the sea, often from farm fertilizer or sewage. The algae spread in thick mats that block sunlight and use up oxygen, which is bad news for the coral underneath.

To stifle something is to smother it so it cannot grow, spread or come out. You can stifle a yawn in class, and a rule can stifle an argument before it starts. Here the algae spread over the reef and block the light the coral needs, so the coral's growth is stifled.

Overfishing means catching so many of a kind of sea creature that not enough are left to breed and replace the ones taken, so the population shrinks year after year. On a reef it matters twice over. Some of the fish being caught are the ones that eat the algae smothering the coral.

A penchant is a strong liking for something, a taste you keep going back to. You might have a penchant for horror films or for salty snacks. Here certain sea creatures have a penchant for eating coral, meaning coral is what they go for given the choice.

The Georgia Institute of Technology, usually called Georgia Tech, is a university in Atlanta, in the United States, known for science and engineering research. The two scientists in this story, Cody Clements and Mark Hay, work there. Universities are where most research like this experiment gets done.

You usually meet candidate in elections, where it means a person running for a job. It has a wider meaning too: anything at all that might fit a description. Calling sea cucumbers an unlikely candidate for the list means nobody expected them to belong on it.

Cylindrical means shaped like a cylinder: a tube with rounded ends, the shape of a soup can or a rolled-up poster. The word comes straight from cylinder. Sea cucumbers get their name because they really do look like soft fat tubes lying on the sea floor.

Armour is a hard covering that protects a body, like a knight's metal suit or a beetle's shell, and unarmoured means going without one. Sea urchins have spines and starfish have tough knobbly skin, but their relative the sea cucumber is soft all over. This is the British spelling; Americans write unarmored.

A sea urchin is a small round sea animal covered in sharp spines, like a living pincushion stuck to a rock. Urchins, starfish and sea cucumbers all belong to the same family group of spiny-skinned sea animals. That is why the article puts them side by side.

Sediment is the loose material that settles to the bottom of water and sits there: sand, mud, grit and bits of dead plants and animals. Rivers, lakes and the sea all collect it. A sea cucumber crawls along swallowing sediment, takes in the food scraps mixed through it, and pushes the leftover sand out the other end.

Organic matter is anything that was once part of a living thing: dead leaves, scraps of animal, droppings, tiny dead sea creatures. In science organic does not mean healthy or pesticide-free, it means built from the carbon-based molecules living bodies are made of. That dead material mixed into sea-floor sediment is what a sea cucumber lives on.

Therein is an old-fashioned, formal way of saying in that thing or in there. Writers use it so they do not have to repeat what they just named. Digesting the organic matter therein means digesting the food that is in the sediment.

To void something is to empty it out or push it out. Here it is the polite scientific word for going to the bathroom: the sea cucumber swallows sediment, keeps the food in it, and voids the clean sand behind it. Reefs actually depend on this, because sea cucumbers pass tons of sand through their bodies.

Bêche-de-mer is the name for sea cucumber prepared as food, usually gutted, boiled and then dried. The name is French, from an older Portuguese phrase meaning sea worm, and it is said roughly besh-duh-MAIR. Dried this way it keeps for a long time and ships anywhere, which is part of why the trade reaches across the world.

A guise is the form or appearance something takes, especially when it is not the usual one. A superhero in the guise of an ordinary student is the same person in a different outfit. In the guise of bêche-de-mer means the sea cucumber turns up as a dried food product rather than as a live animal.

A delicacy is a food people treat as special and expensive, usually because it is rare or hard to get. What counts as one depends completely on where you live. Dried sea cucumber is a prized delicacy in parts of east Asia, which is why so many are taken off the sea floor.

East Asia is the eastern part of the continent of Asia: China, Japan, the two Koreas, Mongolia and Taiwan. It is where most of the demand for dried sea cucumber comes from. Reefs on the far side of the world are being emptied to supply it.

To monitor something is to watch it steadily over time and keep a record of what you see. A poorly monitored trade is one nobody is really keeping track of, so no one knows how many animals are being taken. That makes it very hard to tell when a species is running out.

A regulated activity is one governments control with rules: who is allowed to do it, how much they may take, what they have to report. Fishing is usually regulated with catch limits and seasons. The sea cucumber trade is poorly regulated, meaning the rules are weak or nobody enforces them.

Bn is short for billion, so $1.5bn means one and a half billion dollars, which is 1,500 million. That is roughly what people around the world pay for dried sea cucumbers in a single year. A number that large explains why the fishing keeps going even when reefs suffer for it.

Conservationists are people whose work is protecting wild places, plants and animals from damage. The word comes from conserve, meaning to keep something from being used up. They are the ones raising the alarm about how many sea cucumbers are being taken.

Stripping something means taking everything of one kind off it and leaving none behind, the way you strip a bed of its sheets. Stripping reefs of their cucumbers means fishing until there are none left there. The worry in this article is what else stops working once they are gone.

Aquaria is the formal plural of aquarium, a tank of water where sea creatures are kept. You can also just say aquariums. Experiments in aquaria happen in tanks in a lab where everything is controlled, which is not at all the same as testing an idea out in the open sea.

To excrete is to release waste out of a body: sweat, urine, droppings. Waste from one living thing is often raw material for another. Sea cucumbers excrete ammonia and carbonate into the water around them, and both turn out to help the coral nearby.

Ammonia is a chemical made of nitrogen and hydrogen, the sharp-smelling stuff in some household cleaners. Animals release it as waste when they break down protein. Plants and algae can take it back in and use the nitrogen in it to build protein of their own, so one animal's waste becomes another living thing's supplies.

Carbonate is a chemical unit made of carbon and oxygen, and an ion is an atom or small group of atoms carrying an electric charge. Carbonate is the building block of chalky material: eggshells, seashells and coral skeletons are mostly calcium carbonate. Carbonate ions floating in seawater make it less acidic and give coral the material it needs to build with.

In chemistry a compound is a substance made of two or more different elements joined together, like water joining hydrogen and oxygen. It is not a mixture you could pick apart by hand, because the atoms are bonded. Ammonia is a compound of nitrogen and hydrogen. The word has other meanings elsewhere, such as a walled group of buildings.

Nitrogen is a chemical element, the gas that makes up about four-fifths of the air you are breathing right now. Living things need nitrogen to build protein, but almost none of them can take it straight from the air. They have to get it from a compound such as ammonia instead, which is why ammonia in the water matters so much to algae.

Hydrogen is the lightest chemical element and the most common substance in the universe. On Earth it is nearly always joined to something else: two hydrogen atoms plus one oxygen atom make water. Joined to nitrogen instead, it makes ammonia.

Symbiotic describes two different kinds of living thing that live together closely, usually with each side gaining something. The algae here live inside the coral animals. The algae get a sheltered sunny spot and raw materials, and in return most of the sugar they make from sunlight passes into the animal. Scientists call the arrangement symbiosis, from Greek words meaning living together.

Algae are simple plant-like living things with no roots, stems or flowers. They run from the green slime on a pond to seaweed meters long, and like plants they use sunlight to make sugars. The microscopic ones living inside coral animals are what feed a whole reef.

A sea anemone is a soft sea animal fixed to a rock, with a ring of stinging tentacles waving above it so that it looks rather like a flower. Coral animals are close relatives, built to the same plan but much smaller and each sitting inside a hard stony case. Calling them sea-anemone-like is the quickest way to picture what a coral animal really is.

Anthozoans are the group of sea animals that includes corals and sea anemones. The name comes from Greek words meaning flower animals, because of the way their tentacles fan out. Each reef-building anthozoan is only a few millimeters across, and the reef is the stone they leave behind.

Acidity is how acidic a liquid is, measured on a scale chemists call pH. Higher acidity dissolves chalky material like shells and coral skeletons. When sea cucumbers release carbonate they lower the acidity of the water right around them, so the coral there has an easier time building.

French Polynesia is a group of over a hundred islands scattered across the South Pacific Ocean and governed as part of France; Tahiti is the best known of them. The islands sit in warm tropical water ringed by coral reefs. That is why reef scientists travel there to work.

To decamp is to pack up and leave one place for another. It began as an army word, meaning to break camp and move on. The two researchers decamped to French Polynesia, which is to say they left their lab in Georgia and moved the whole operation to the Pacific.

Mo’orea is a small volcanic island in French Polynesia, right next to Tahiti, and its name is said roughly moh-oh-RAY-ah. A coral reef runs all the way around it in shallow water, and there is a research station on the island, so scientists can dive down to their experiments within minutes. That is where the twenty cages were set out.

A fringe is a border running along the edge of something, like the fringe on a rug. Reefs fringing the island means reefs forming a border right along its shoreline. Scientists actually use the term fringing reef for this kind, as opposed to reefs that sit further out to sea.

To double down is to commit even harder to something instead of backing away, especially after it has not worked yet. The phrase comes from a bet in the card game blackjack where you double your stake. The scientists got no result from their first experiment and, rather than give up, ran a bigger one.

Encaged simply means put inside a cage. The prefix en- turns a noun into a verb meaning to put into that thing: encircle, entomb, encage. The encaged coral species are the ones growing inside the experiment's cages.

Staghorn coral grows in branching arms that look like the antlers of a stag, which is a male deer. It grows fast and builds much of the structure reef fish shelter in, and it is also among the corals most easily killed by hot water and disease. Many staghorn species are now endangered.

Acropora pulchra is the scientific two-part name of one staghorn coral species. Every known living thing has a name like this, usually in Latin, with the first part naming the wider group and the second the exact species, so that scientists anywhere in the world mean the same creature. This is the coral that grew 41 percent faster with sea cucumbers nearby.

Whopping is an informal word meaning surprisingly big. It goes in front of the thing it describes, as in a whopping 41 percent or a whopping great sandwich. Using it here tells you the writer thinks that result is far larger than anyone expected.

In everyday speech significant just means important. In science it means something stricter: a result clear enough that it probably is not down to luck. Two of three coral species growing faster is a significant result, meaning the effect looks real rather than an accident of which corals happened to sit in which cage.

When something bears on a question, it has a direct effect on the answer. This bear has nothing to do with the animal; it is the older sense meaning to carry or press. The experiment bears directly on whether the sea cucumber trade needs controlling, because it shows what happens to coral once the cucumbers are gone.

Urgency is the quality of needing to be dealt with right now rather than later. It is the noun that goes with urgent. If losing sea cucumbers harms coral too, then bringing the trade under control is more urgent than people had thought.
